questions.question: What is a polynomial on $\mathbb{R}^n$?
options: A real-valued function that is a finite sum of monomials on $\mathbb{R}^n$
Any function from $\mathbb{R}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$ with all partial derivatives
A sequence of real numbers indexed by $n$
A function whose graph is always a straight line

questions.question: How is the degree of a polynomial on $\mathbb{R}^n$ determined?
options: By the smallest total degree among its monomials
By the highest total degree among its monomials with nonzero coefficient
By the number of variables that appear in the polynomial
By the number of terms in the finite sum

questions.question: What is the degree of $f(x,y) = x^2+2xy+y^2+x+1$?
Which expression is a polynomial on $\mathbb{R}^2$?
options: $\dfrac{1}{x}+y$
$\sin(x)+y$
$\sqrt{x}+y^2$

questions.question: If $p$ and $q$ are polynomials, what is true about the degree of $p+q$?
options: It is always the sum of the degrees of $p$ and $q$
It is always the minimum of the degrees of $p$ and $q$
It is at most the maximum of the degrees of $p$ and $q$
It is undefined unless $p$ and $q$ have the same degree

questions.question: What can be said about partial derivatives of a polynomial on $\mathbb{R}^n$?
options: Only first-order partial derivatives exist
All partial derivatives of all orders exist and are polynomials or zero
Partial derivatives exist only at interior points of bounded sets
Partial derivatives exist, but need not be real-valued

questions.question: Let $p(x,y) = x^2+y$ and $q(x,y) = xy^3$. What is the degree of $p q$?
For $f(x,y,z) = x^2yz+z^3+y$, what is the degree of $f$?
Why does the degree of $p+q$ need the phrase 'at most'?
options: Because a polynomial may contain infinitely many monomials
Because a product of polynomials may have smaller degree
Because the number of variables always changes under addition
Because the highest-degree terms may cancel in the sum

questions.question: Which statement correctly connects polynomials on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with monomials on $\mathbb{R}^n$?
options: Every polynomial is one monomial of total degree $n$
Every polynomial is a finite combination of monomials
Every monomial is excluded from being a polynomial
Every polynomial must contain every possible monomial up to its degree

questions.question: Let $p(x,y) = x^2+y$ and $q(x,y) = -x^2+y^3$. What is the degree of $p+q$?
For $f(x,y) = x^3+xy+y^2$, which second partial derivative is zero?
options: $\dfrac{\partial^2 f}{\partial y^2}$
$\dfrac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x\partial y}$
$\dfrac{\partial^4 f}{\partial y^4}$
$\dfrac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2}$

questions.question: Which description defines a polynomial on $\mathbb{R}^n$?
options: An infinite product of trigonometric functions.
A single point in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
A finite sum of monomials on $\mathbb{R}^n$.
Any discontinuous real-valued function.

questions.question: Which monomial degree determines the degree of a polynomial on $\mathbb{R}^n$?
options: By the number of variables only.
By the smallest coefficient.
By the maximum total degree among its monomials.
By the value of the polynomial at the origin.

questions.question: Which regularity property is stated for polynomials on $\mathbb{R}^n$?
options: They are never differentiable.
They are differentiable only at the origin.
They are infinitely differentiable.
They have no partial derivatives.

questions.question: What is the degree of $f(x,y)=x^3y+xy^2+1$?
What is the degree of $f(x,y)=x^3+xy+y^2$?
Which expression is a polynomial in two real variables?
options: $\sin x+y$
$\dfrac{1}{x}+y$
$\sqrt{x}+y^2$

questions.question: What is the degree of the product of two polynomials?
options: At most the maximum of their degrees.
Always zero.
The sum of their degrees.
Always one.

questions.question: If $p$ has degree $2$ and $q$ has degree $5$, what is the degree of $pq$?
